newsitem.title: INDIA: India to bring its crude prices in line with world.
newsitem.headline: India to bring its crude prices in line with world.

text.p: The Indian government will announce a new exploration policy within two months which will bring the domestic prices of crude petroleum in line with world prices, a senior official said on Friday.

"The government within two months will come out with a new exploration policy to provide a level playing field for public and private sector companies wherein the prices of crude to be paid to the government and private companies will be at par with international prices," Devi Dayal, additional secretary in the Petroleum Ministry, told a petroleum technology conference.
Currently domestic Indian crude prices are far below world prices.
Dayal said that under the new exploration policy, "government companies (will) also have to bid for acreage for exploration and production".
He said "a new fiscal regime is being evolved in which there will be substantial concessions for exploration in frontier areas and deep waters".
Domestic crude is currently priced at about $11 to $12 a barrel, compared to about $22 to $23 on international markets.
